# vercel_project_protection_inventory (Data Source)

Reads protection bypasses and access exceptions visible through the public project and alias APIs, without creating, adopting, or revoking them. Includes automation and integration bypasses, URL exceptions, shareable links, individual access, OPTIONS paths, and Trusted Sources, including implicit self-access and Vercel CI access. Bearer secrets and secret-bearing URLs are not stored in state.

This is a snapshot of visible configuration, not a guarantee that a deployment is protected. The public APIs do not establish coverage of deployment-owned access without alias records or guarantee complete visibility for the API token, so complete is currently always false. Missing access maps are reported in incomplete_reasons. Failed requests, invalid JSON, and unsupported Trusted Sources or OPTIONS fields fail the read instead of returning an empty inventory. Expired links, pending requests, invitations, and explicit empty Trusted Sources rules remain in the inventory.

For trusted-project entries, null custom_allow means default matching-environment access (plus development to preview for self-access); an empty set means no access. Vercel CI same-repository access permits same-team CI to preview and production deployments built from the CI repository. This defaults to enabled when not stored. These defaults are access routes even when no explicit exception has been configured.

Approval keys identify the observed access configuration, including credential rotation, target identity, and rule changes. They exclude notes and audit timestamps. They are versioned SHA-256 fingerprints, not API IDs or credentials. Terraform postconditions can reject unapproved entries, but cannot prevent later dashboard changes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "vercel_project_protection_inventory" "example" {
  project_id = "prj_example"
  team_id    = "team_example"
}

output "protection_access" {
  value = data.vercel_project_protection_inventory.example.entries
}
```

## Optional plan assertions

To reject visible entries that have not been approved, add a postcondition. Copy approved keys from a reviewed inventory into your configuration; do not build the approval list automatically from the same live inventory.

```terraform
# Optional: reject visible entries that have not been approved.
# This does not establish full coverage: complete is currently always false.
variable "approved_protection_entries" {
  type    = set(string)
  default = []
}

data "vercel_project_protection_inventory" "approved" {
  project_id = "prj_example"
  team_id    = "team_example"

  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition = alltrue([
        for entry in self.entries :
        contains(var.approved_protection_entries, entry.approval_key)
      ])
      error_message = "Unapproved protection access exists."
    }
  }
}
```

This checks all reported entries, including expired links, pending requests, explicit denies and implicit defaults. It does not prove that no other access exists. To require full coverage too, add a separate postcondition with `condition = self.complete`; that condition currently always fails because public API coverage is incomplete.

These assertions fail during planning when the data source is read during planning. Keep project and team inputs known and avoid dependencies on pending changes, which can defer the read to apply. Use a normal plan with refresh enabled; this is an observation of current access, not continuous enforcement.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) The project ID. Names are not accepted so inventory identity survives project renames.

### Optional

- `team_id` (String) The team ID. Defaults to the provider's team.

### Read-Only

- `complete` (Boolean) Whether all project access routes are covered. Currently always false because public API coverage and token visibility are not guaranteed.
- `entries` (Attributes Set) Observed access entries, including implicit defaults and inactive entries. Entries are not filtered by their status. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries))
- `id` (String) The project ID.
- `incomplete_reasons` (Set of String) Known limitations and missing access metadata. An empty entries set must not be interpreted as no exceptions when this set is nonempty.

<a id="nestedatt--entries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries`

Read-Only:

- `alias` (String) Alias hostname, without a query string, or null for project access.
- `approval_key` (String) Versioned fingerprint of the team, project, target, credential or subject, and access configuration. Changes when access changes.
- `claims` (Map of Set of String) Required OIDC claims and accepted values for trusted-oidc access. Values are ORed within each claim; claims are ANDed.
- `configuration_id` (String) Integration configuration ID for integration-created automation access.
- `created_at` (Number) Creation time in Unix milliseconds, when returned by the API.
- `created_by` (String) Creator ID, when returned by the API.
- `custom_allow` (Attributes Set) Custom environment rules for trusted-project access. Null uses defaults; an empty set explicitly denies access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--custom_allow))
- `expires_at` (Number) Expiry time in Unix seconds, or null when no expiry was returned.
- `implicit` (Boolean) Whether this entry represents implicit self-access or a Vercel CI default rather than an explicit rule.
- `integration_id` (String) Integration ID for integration-created automation access.
- `is_env_var` (Boolean) Whether an automation bypass is the deployment environment variable default. Omitted legacy values are interpreted as true. Null for other scopes.
- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer for trusted-oidc access.
- `last_updated_at` (Number) Last update time in Unix milliseconds, when returned by the API.
- `last_updated_by` (String) Last updater ID, when returned by the API.
- `note` (String) Display note or Trusted Source label, when returned by the API. Not used for approval identity.
- `path_prefix` (String) Path prefix bypassed for OPTIONS requests, or null for other scopes.
- `scope` (String) API bypass scope, or options-allowlist, trusted-project, trusted-oidc, or vercel-ci-same-repository. Unrecognized API scopes are retained with unknown status.
- `status` (String) active, expired, granted, requested, invited, disabled, or unknown. Active describes configuration, not whether protection currently applies to a URL. Invitations are not treated as confirmed grants.
- `subject` (String) The user or email map key for individual access, or null for other scopes. Bearer map keys are never returned.
- `target_id` (String) The project or alias ID owning this entry.
- `target_type` (String) The owner of the entry: project or alias.
- `to` (Attributes) Allowed target environments for trusted-oidc access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--to))
- `trusted_project_id` (String) Source project ID for trusted-project access.

<a id="nestedatt--entries--custom_allow"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries.custom_allow`

Read-Only:

- `from` (Attributes) The source environments on the trusted project that are allowed to access the target environments. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--custom_allow--from))
- `to` (Attributes) The target environments on this project that may be accessed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--custom_allow--to))

<a id="nestedatt--entries--custom_allow--from"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries.custom_allow.from`

Read-Only:

- `preset` (String) Named environment preset. Currently only `all-custom` is supported.
- `slugs` (Set of String) System environment slugs (`production`, `preview`, `development`) or custom environment slugs.


<a id="nestedatt--entries--custom_allow--to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries.custom_allow.to`

Read-Only:

- `preset` (String) Named environment preset. Currently only `all-custom` is supported.
- `slugs` (Set of String) System environment slugs (`production`, `preview`, `development`) or custom environment slugs.



<a id="nestedatt--entries--to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries.to`

Read-Only:

- `preset` (String) Named environment preset. Currently only `all-custom` is supported.
- `slugs` (Set of String) System environment slugs (`production`, `preview`, `development`) or custom environment slugs.
